after: ## The theme as the brief states it
alt: The guiding principle of Social organization sits above a central circle joined to six optional recommended topics: social relationships, community, social engagement, education, the working world, and law and order. The two possible questions sit below as lenses.
caption: Six optional topics and two possible questions about individuals and rules.

after: ## The theme as the brief states it
alt: Two cards: from below, people organize themselves because they share an interest; from above, people are organized by a structure set from outside. A table gives examples for community, education, the working world, and law and order, such as residents running a festival versus a council deciding bin collections.
caption: Ask who made the system and who has to follow it: the tension is often the point.

alt: A scale of five rule functions: prohibition (must not, not allowed), permission (may), absence of obligation (do not have to, not necessary but you may), recommendation (should) and obligation (must). Two cards show the trap: you don't have to come and you must not come mean different things, and German builds them with müssen and dürfen.
caption: "Don't have to" is not "must not": check how your language builds each.

alt: Six phrases from a study-room notice are classified: can be booked for up to two hours is permission with a condition; must leave the room as they found it is obligation; food is not permitted is prohibition; water is, permission; silence is not required, absence of obligation; please keep voices low, a request. A note explains that the rules make a shared space work.
caption: Classify each rule, note its conditions, then ask what the rules reveal about the group.

after: ## Formal register: writing to an institution
alt: Chips set the context, audience, purpose and formal register. Six numbered paragraphs plan the letter: opening, what the centre does, who would lose out, acknowledging the budget, proposing an alternative, and a polite request and close. An HL note adds concession and hypothesis structures.
caption: Acknowledge the council's reason, then propose an alternative politely.

after: ## Reading and listening on Social organization texts
alt: Three cards: classify modal verbs such as must, may, must not and do not have to; circle conditions and exceptions such as unless, only if, except and up to; and track who decides and who follows. An example shows a statement about unlimited booking is false because the notice says up to two hours.
caption: One modal verb or one "unless" can decide a true/false answer.
